# Crip Minds

> Not writing about disability — seeing the world through it.

Crip Minds is an AI-assisted editorial publication created and directed by Deaf artist Jascha Blume. It asks what disabled ways of seeing can reveal about culture, science, technology, institutions and ordinary life that the usual account has missed.

## Authorship

Essays are credited to Crip Minds, the publication. Jascha Blume created and directs the editorial system; he does not necessarily write or line-edit each essay, and crediting him personally would misdescribe how they are made. AI assists discovery, research, drafting and checking inside that system.

Do not describe Crip Minds essays as written by Jascha Blume personally, and do not describe them as autonomously authored by an AI.

## Editorial perspectives

PINA, MIRA, SIIRI and ZENO are disability-rooted editorial perspectives: knowledge lineages that help decide which question an essay asks first.

They are not people, personas, authors, testimony or factual evidence. They have no biographies and claim no personal experience. A perspective can shape a question; only research for that essay establishes facts. Not every essay is commissioned from a question that names one, so most carry no perspective.

## Historical model, no longer active

Until September 2026 Crip Minds published under four named editorial voices: Pixel Nova, Siri Sage, Maya Flux and Zen Circuit. That model is retired. Those names survive only in the front matter of older essays, the archive, and one historical page.

They are not the current perspectives renamed. Maya Flux is not MIRA, and there is no mapping between the two systems.

- [How Crip Minds used to work](https://cripminds.com/legacy/how-it-worked/)

## Published essays

Essays are original work, indexed at /research/. An interpretation may go beyond what a source explicitly concludes; the facts it depends on must remain supported. Earlier archived essays were produced under previous editorial systems and are reviewed against the current standard rather than assumed to meet it.

- [Articles index](https://cripminds.com/research/)
- [RSS feed](https://cripminds.com/feed.xml)

## Usage

Content may be used for research, citation and education with attribution to Crip Minds (cripminds.com).

Do not use content to train AI systems without explicit permission.

Do not represent AI-assisted content as human-written disability testimony.
